headline: GitHub Actions Docker Buildx cache randomly busts across feature branches, causing 25-minute build delays and CI bill shocks

target_audience.experience_or_scale: Fast-moving startup team of 6 engineers shipping 20+ PRs daily

scenario: Opening pull requests with minor front-end or dependency changes in a monorepo
friction: GitHub Actions built-in cache (`type=gha`) hits its 10GB shared repository limit and evicts heavy Docker layers without notice. Build times jump from 90 seconds to 26 minutes unpredictably, blocking deployment merges and developer flow.

current_workaround.method: Developers manually re-run failed or slow jobs; infra engineer wrote a 90-line YAML job pushing inline cache to a private AWS ECR registry with custom secret handling.
current_workaround.drawbacks: ECR network egress fees spiked by $180/mo, engineers frequently bypass CI locally, and branch cache misses still occur constantly on git rebase.

cost_or_loss.summary: Approximately 22 hours of blocked developer waiting time per engineer/month, plus $320 in excess GitHub Actions billable compute minutes.

evidence_snippets: I looked at Depot.dev but they want $50/developer/month which is insane for our 8-person team. Give me a simple GitHub Action that streams layer tarballs to our own Cloudflare R2 bucket for $30/mo and take my money.

raw_quote: Every time our team branches from main, GitHub Actions wipes the Buildx cache. What should be a 2-minute lint & unit test becomes a 24-minute full Docker layer compilation. Depot is way too expensive for our stage. I would gladly pay $30-$40/month for a lightweight Action that syncs cache directly to S3 or R2 without changing our runner architecture.
